newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to mostly higher.

text.p: Med oil products were steady to mostly higher on Wednesday after recent sharp gains in crude and products futures.

Gas oil gained $1.25 a tonne on firmer futures but premiums were unchanged in slow business. The emergence of fresh Romanian, Italian and French demand for heating oil was insufficient to dispel the market's weak tone.
A 25,000 tonne Russian was sold at high cif quotes +$0.75 loading Dec 10-11 ex-Tuapse, around unchanged.
Another Russian offered loading Dec 15-18 at equivalent to high cif quotes +$1.30 was cited by traders as a harbinger of a stronger market later in the month.

High sulphur cracked fuel faced both bullish and bearish pressure on Wednesday. Some dealers felt the recent push upwards had been overplayed and thought there was a concerted effort by some players to hike prices higher. A cargo was heard offered at $114.50 fob Med.
"Far too high when there are up to six ISAB cargoes in December," said a trader at a major, seeing the market $2 lower.

The bulls cited the Portuguese tender for 75,000 tonnes in December and January, which was won by Stinnes, and the Turkish buy tender for 45,000-50,0000 tonnes, which is awarded on Friday Dec 6. A bunker spec Greek cargo was understood sold around high cif quotes +$2.
Naphtha prices rose about $2 to $229/$231, tracking firmer NWE values and recent gains in crude and gasoline.

One source said demand appeared lacklustre in the Med, which may be one an end user was moving a cargo from Tunisia to NWE. Others said it was to meet pent up demand from the closure of Algeria's Skikda port, which reopened on Wednesday.
